implementation.targetScope: Seventeen components: button controls, Typography, Link, SvgIcon, Box, Paper, Divider, Icon, FormControl, FormLabel and FormHelperText; createSvgIcon and the scoped resolved-theme bridge. Includes shared input focus/filled/required/error state, native label and helper accessibility, form theme overrides, surfaces/elevations, horizontal/vertical and labelled dividers, font-icon fallback, current custom-root props, nested/CSS-variable themes and responsive sx. Full Material theme creation and remaining families are not implemented.
implementation.remainingWork: InputBase/Input/OutlinedInput/InputLabel/TextField and remaining form controls; remaining surfaces and data display; navigation, menus, tabs and overlays; full Material theme creation and remaining app-used exports; whole-app integration and consumer release.

changes: Written independently over VPM System and its styling closure; no upstream Material runtime, Babel or prop-types ships.
Native button semantics and direct React rendering; no imperative HTML insertion.
Owned refs and ripple timers are released on unmount; theme changes retain control DOM.
Independent Typography, Link and SvgIcon plus createSvgIcon; no Material runtime dependency. Actual current/app Material icon modules render unchanged above the VPM factory.
Retains Material 7 paragraph, direct system props and CSS/palette-path colors needed by existing callers alongside the current typography contract. Physical text alignment is preserved in RTL.

Explicit root accessibility attributes override nested SVG attributes; titleAccess promotes a decorative SVG child to a named image unless the root explicitly hides it. Prototype-named variants and sizes do not read inherited object properties.

Custom component roots receive native button type/disabled semantics by default, matching Material 9; nativeButton:false explicitly selects ARIA semantics. Browser acceptance covers the application combination of IconButton, motion.button, inherited variants, theme rerenders and ref cleanup.

Independent Material Box and scoped theme bridge, including $$material isolation, nested callback providers and CSS-variable themes. Retains direct System props used by app 7.2.0, which current Material 9 removed. Fuse-style SVG sprite roots are browser checked.
Independent Paper, Divider and Icon use VPM System. Standard shadow geometry is design data obtained from the public default-theme API; no upstream component runtime is copied.

Paper preserves caller shadow/overlay variables and theme overrides; invalid noninteger or out-of-range elevations reject explicitly. Divider preserves separator roles/orientation and legacy app light/vertical-children hooks. Font icons remain decorative unless explicitly exposed.

Box now forwards custom-root API props such as Icon color/fontSize instead of consuming them as System styles, matching Material 9. App Material 7 has the collision; the browser fixture asserts this intentional difference. Native roots retain app direct System props.

Independent FormControl state provider and useFormControl; FormLabel and FormHelperText inherit only undefined options, preserve explicit false, expose native label/helper semantics and reset stale focus on disable. Initial filled/adornment state supports recognized Input/Select children for SSR. Shared provider identity across CJS/ESM context entries; no upstream input code ships.

caller.scope: Navigation actions, contest forms, family area/reminder toggles, palette selector and navbar Fab. Building this subset does not switch VentiMath dependencies. Navigation search and link roots, theme typography and icon sizing, and @mui/icons-material consumers in MustangMath, I2MC and IMO. FuseSvgIcon instead uses styled Box, SVG sprite references and an Icon fallback. Material icons and FuseSvgIcon are distinct callers. Shared external-link actions combine IconButton with motion.button and inherited variants. Paper appears in contest registration/results and public authentication panels; Divider in shared navigation and vertical toolbars; Icon in palette selection and FuseSvgIcon’s non-SVG fallback. Form foundations are used by FuseSettings number/radio/switch controllers and palette selection; the shared theme changes label typography, control color and helper margins. Browser checks use synthetic settings forms and unchanged upstream InputBase through a test-only context bridge.
